t: The first motor policy issued in England in 1895 covered which risk?
e: The 1895 English policy covered third party liability only; a comprehensive policy including own damage followed in 1899.

t: The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 replaced the 1939 Act and came into force on
e: The 1988 Act became effective from 1 July 1989; 09.08.2019 is the date of the 2019 Amendment Act.

t: After detariffing of motor business from 1 January 2007, which element continues to be regulated by IRDAI?
e: Detariffing freed only rates and discounts on OD; TP liability premium, policy wordings and terms remain regulated.

t: A transport vehicle driving licence issued under Section 10 remains valid for
e: Transport vehicle licences are valid for 5 years; the age-linked durations apply to non-transport classes.

t: A driver aged 45 years obtains an LMV (non-transport) licence. For how long is it effective?
e: For a driver above 30 but below 50 years at issue, a non-transport licence is valid for 10 years.

t: A private car driver's licence expired 14 months before the accident and was never renewed. For claim purposes the officer should treat the licence as
o: Effective, since renewal is possible within 5 years
Effective, since a grace period of 2 years applies
Not effective; renewal beyond one year requires a fresh test
Effective only for the OD section
e: Under Section 15, renewal applied within one year of expiry is permitted; beyond one year the authority must refuse unless the applicant passes the test again.

t: On sale of a vehicle registered in the same State, the seller must report the transfer to the RTO within
e: Section 50 requires the transferor to report within 14 days (45 days if registered in another State); the transferee applies within 30 days.

t: India Motor Tariff endorsements (IMTs) are contained in which section of the Motor Tariff?
e: Section 7 holds the IMT endorsements; Section 6 has standard wordings and Section 8 statistical codes.

t: The minimum age for obtaining a licence to drive a motor cycle not exceeding 50 cc is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Section 10 permits a licence for motor cycles up to 50 cc at 16 years; geared motor cycles and LMV require 18 and transport vehicles 20.

t: Under GR-4, geographical area extension of a Package Policy to Nepal and Bhutan is charged at
e: Extension to Bangladesh, Bhutan, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Maldives costs a flat ₹500 for Package and ₹100 for other policies.

t: A car manufactured in 1935 and certified by the Vintage and Classic Car Club of India is entitled to
o: 25% discount on OD and 50% on TP premium
50% discount on OD and 25% on TP premium
e: GR-5 vintage cars (manufactured prior to 31.12.1940) get 25% OD and 50% TP discount; classic cars get no special rating.

t: A private car has an IDV of ₹4,00,000. The surveyor assesses repair cost at ₹3,20,000. The claim should be treated as
o: Constructive total loss, since repair cost exceeds 75% of IDV
e: Repair cost is 80% of IDV; GR-8 treats the vehicle as CTL when aggregate retrieval/repair cost exceeds 75% of IDV.

t: Under GR-9, depreciation applicable on fibre glass components in a partial loss claim is
e: Fibre glass components attract 30%; rubber/plastic/tyres/batteries/airbags attract 50%, glass nil, other parts as per age.

t: Metal parts worth ₹40,000 are replaced on a car aged 3 years 8 months. The depreciation deducted on these parts is
e: For a vehicle above 3 years but below 4 years, depreciation on metal parts is 25%, i.e. ₹10,000.

t: For a private car registered at Pune, the rating zone under GR-10 is
e: For private cars and two wheelers, Zone A comprises Ahmedabad, Bangalore, Chennai, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Mumbai, New Delhi and Pune.

t: Under Section 19, on a first offence referred by the licensing authority, the driver may be disqualified from holding a licence for
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). First offence attracts disqualification of 3 months; a second or subsequent offence leads to revocation, and a refresher course is required before return of the licence.

t: A goods carrying truck registered at Jaipur (a State capital) falls in
e: For commercial vehicles (other than 4.C.1/4.C.4), Zone A is the four metros, Zone B all other State capitals and Zone C the rest of India.

t: Short period cover or renewal under GR-12 is not permissible for
e: GR-12 notes that short period covers and renewals are not permissible for Liability Only policies.

t: The minimum premium per vehicle for a vehicle specially modified for use of a handicapped person is
e: GR-16 prescribes ₹25 for vehicles designed/modified for blind, handicapped or mentally challenged persons and ₹100 for all other vehicles.

t: A cover note under GR-22 is issued in which form and is valid for how long?
e: Cover notes are in Form 52 under Rule 142(1) CMVR 1989 and are valid for 60 days; Form 51 is the certificate of insurance.

t: When the insurer cancels a motor policy, it must give notice by recorded delivery of
e: GR-24: insurer cancels with 7 days notice and refunds pro-rata premium; cancellation at the insured's request retains premium on short period scale.

t: Own damage premium is ₹12,000 and the insured has completed four consecutive claim-free years. The NCB amount is
e: NCB after 4 completed claim-free years is 45%; 45% of ₹12,000 is ₹6,600.

t: A policy expired on 1 March and the insured approaches for renewal on 15 June of the same year. His NCB entitlement is
o: Nil, as renewal is beyond 90 days of expiry
Retained if a no-claim declaration is given
e: GR-27: no NCB is allowed if the policy is not renewed within 90 days of expiry (365 days only for military personnel in forward areas with a declaration).

t: On accepting an NCB declaration from a new customer, the insurer must write to the previous insurer within
e: The granting insurer must write within 21 days and the previous insurer must confirm within 30 days; failure by either is a breach of tariff.

t: OD premium on a private car is ₹6,000 and the insured is an Automobile Association member. The AA discount allowed is
e: GR-28 allows 5% of OD premium (₹300) subject to a maximum of ₹200 for cars (₹50 for two wheelers).

t: Anti-theft device discount under GR-30 requires the device to be approved by
e: The device must be ARAI-approved and its installation certified by an Automobile Association; discount is 2.5% of OD premium up to ₹500.

t: Section 56 provides that a transport vehicle whose fitness certificate has expired shall
o: Continue to be validly registered for 30 days
Be treated as a non-transport vehicle
Not be deemed validly registered under Section 39
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Without a valid certificate of fitness a transport vehicle is not deemed to be validly registered, which has direct bearing on claim admissibility.

t: Concession for a laid-up vehicle under GR-31 is available only if the vehicle is not in use for at least
e: The lay-up must be not less than 2 consecutive months, with prior written notice, surrender of the certificate and ₹15 administration charge.

t: The capital sum insured under the compulsory PA cover for owner-driver is
e: GR-36 as revised prescribes CSI of ₹15 lakh for the owner-driver CPA cover.

t: A private car is owned by a partnership firm. The compulsory PA cover for owner-driver should be
o: Granted in the name of the managing partner
Granted with CSI of ₹2 lakh only
Not granted and no premium charged
Granted only for the paid driver
e: CPA cover cannot be granted where the vehicle is owned by a company, firm or body corporate, or where the owner has no effective licence; the provision is deleted and no premium charged.

t: The TPPD limit under a two wheeler policy, unless restricted to the statutory limit, is
e: GR-39: ₹1 lakh for private and commercial two wheelers; ₹7.5 lakh for all other vehicles; the insured may opt to restrict to the statutory limit at inception.

t: A private car of 1800 cc has an assessed OD loss of ₹25,000 after depreciation. The amount payable after compulsory deductible is
e: GR-40 compulsory deductible for private cars exceeding 1500 cc is ₹2,000, so ₹23,000 is payable.

t: The compulsory deductible for a goods carrying vehicle of 12,000 kg GVW is
e: GCVs above 7,500 kg and up to 16,500 kg GVW carry ₹1,000; below 7,500 kg ₹500; above 16,500 kg ₹1,500.

t: Electrical fittings not included in the manufacturer's selling price are valued at ₹50,000. The additional OD premium under GR-41 is
e: GR-41 charges 4% on the value of such fittings, i.e. ₹2,000, provided they are specifically declared.

t: Under Section 45 of the Insurance Act 1938, a life insurance policy cannot be called in question on any ground after how many years from the date of issue, revival or rider addition, whichever is later?
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). The 2015 amendment made the three-year bar absolute: after three years no policy may be questioned on any ground, including fraud.

t: For a vehicle fitted with a separately valued RTA-approved CNG kit, the additional premium under GR-42 is
o: 4% on the kit value plus ₹60 for TP
5% extra on OD premium plus ₹60 for TP
e: A separately valued kit is insured at 4% of its value for OD, plus ₹60 towards liability; 5% on OD applies only where kit value is not separately available.

t: A car kept in a garage and not in use is to be insured for fire and theft only without liability cover. The premium rate is
e: GR-45A: Fire or Theft alone is 0.50% of IDV; Fire and Theft together is 0.75% of IDV, with a written declaration that the vehicle is garaged.

t: Liability Only Policy with Fire and Theft cover under GR-45B is charged at Liability premium plus
e: Fire only adds 25%, theft only 30% and fire plus theft 50% of the appropriate OD premium, subject to minimum premium.

t: Standard towing charges payable under a private car package policy are limited to
e: Towing limits are ₹300 for two wheelers, ₹750 for three wheelers, ₹1,500 for private cars and ₹2,500 for commercial vehicles.

t: An insured carries out spot repairs on his motor cycle without intimation. Such repairs are permitted up to an estimated cost of
e: Spot repairs are permitted up to ₹500 for other vehicles and ₹150 for motor cycles.

t: On the death of an individual insured, the motor policy remains valid in favour of the legal heirs for
o: 30 days or expiry, whichever is earlier
3 months or expiry, whichever is earlier
e: The policy continues for 3 months from death or until expiry, whichever is earlier, within which heirs must transfer or take a fresh policy.

t: Under the IRDAI Master Circular dated 11.06.2024 cited by the trainer, a surveyor must be appointed for motor OD claims above
e: The 2024 master circular requires surveyor appointment for claims above ₹50,000, allotted within 24 hours on a random tech-based basis.

t: As per the trainer's summary of the 2024 master circular, the insurer must decide a claim within how many days of receiving the survey report?
e: The circular requires the survey report within 15 days and the insurer's decision within 7 days thereafter, followed by immediate payment.

t: Under the survey fee schedule w.e.f. 01.10.2022, the fee for a repair estimate of ₹3,00,000 is
e: For estimates between ₹2 lakh and ₹30 lakh the fee is ₹2,800 plus 0.70% on the balance above ₹2 lakh: 2,800 + 700 = ₹3,500.

t: Which add-on cover pays the difference between the current invoice price and IDV on total loss or theft of a new vehicle?
e: Return to Invoice is available for new vehicles owned by the original buyer, covers invoice price minus IDV and also first registration charges and road tax.

t: The maximum OD liability of the insurer under a Motor Trade Internal Risks (Class G) package policy for any one accident is
e: Class G limits OD to ₹50,000 any one accident; TPPD is ₹1,50,000 and bodily injury unlimited.

t: Section 41 of the Insurance Act 1938 prohibits:
o: Payment of any rebate of premium or commission as an inducement to buy insurance
Issue of a policy without a medical examination
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Section 41 bars rebating; contravention attracts a penalty of up to ₹10 lakh.

t: Under Section 161 of the MV Act as amended in 2019, compensation for death in a hit-and-run accident is
e: Section 161 provides ₹2 lakh for death and ₹50,000 for grievous hurt in hit-and-run cases; ₹5 lakh/₹2.5 lakh are the Section 164 no-fault amounts.

t: An appeal against a MACT award lies to the High Court within
e: Section 173 allows appeal within 90 days, with deposit of ₹25,000 or 50% of the award whichever is less; no appeal if the amount in dispute is below ₹1 lakh.

t: IRDAI's circular of 18 October 2023 directed that IMT-29 cover for employees in an employer's private car be provided
o: As an optional add-on at ₹50 per employee
Compulsorily as inbuilt cover under the TP section at no additional premium
Only under package policies at 5% extra premium
Only for vehicles owned by companies
e: Following Madras High Court directions, IMT-29 became compulsory inbuilt cover under the TP liability section of private car policies with no additional premium until further directions.
